By this point in your life, you've likely already experienced traditional dentistry. Most people go to a general dentist when they get a cavity or toothache. A standard tooth filling, dental crown, or root canal all fall under the umbrella of traditional dental services. While a cosmetic dental office also offers services that can restore your teeth back to health, the dentist's goals also include making them look as natural as possible. Instead of slapping on a metal crown in your smile zone, our cosmetic dentists will evaluate your smile and find the perfect shade of a restoration to match the rest of your teeth.

Removing old metal fillings and replacing them with tooth-colored ones can make it less embarrassing to smile when you once had decay in your smile zone. During our first time meeting, our dentists will take their time to fully explain each aspect of your treatment plan. Then, they'll work with you to develop a timeline for each procedure that works with your schedule.

Does Cosmetic Dentistry Cost a Lot?

Money should never be a barrier to helping you look and feel your best, but we know that people still need to factor in their budgets when they make choices about their cosmetic dental care. The good news is that those feelings of awkwardness when you smile can go away quite quickly when you get dental implants in Pinellas Park. How Do Affordable Dental Implants Work?

The prospect of undergoing dental implant surgery tends to bring up a lot of questions. At its core, a dental implant is a screw-shaped post that is made from hypoallergenic material that we place into your jawbone, which is called an endosteal implant. When there isn't enough bone left in your jaw to support an implant, you could receive a subperiosteal implant that sits above the jawbone line. In either case, the dental implants procedure is meant to help you achieve a replacement tooth that is more stable than removable dentures.

Is the Dental Implants Cost Affordable?

Once you start asking about the dental implants cost, you've likely developed a good grasp on what they are so beneficial for your oral health. Giving you a random estimate of the dental implants cost is difficult, since people tend to have very unique mouths and oral health needs. When you visit our dental office in your area, we can give you an estimate that is based upon your exam results. Affordable dental implants are possible for everyone, and we can help you achieve your goal of making your new tooth replacements fit your budget.

Will Dental Implants Insurance Cover the Cost?

In most cases, dental implants insurance doesn't cover all of the costs of this procedure. But, we've already figured out how to make sure that no one has to opt out of replacing their teeth. If your general dental insurance doesn't cover major parts of the procedure, then we'll step in to see if you might benefit from our flexible financing plans.

Steps Involved With the Dental Implants Procedure

Some people need bone grafting or treatment for gum disease before we begin the dental implants procedure. Following any pre-surgical care, we'll then prepare the area for the implant by doing a gentle cleaning and using anesthesia to help you stay pain-free. Our dentist then uses their expert touch to insert the implant in your bone or gums where it will then begin the process of fusing to your oral tissue and bone to provide support for the crown.

What Are the Biggest Benefits of Implants?

Dental implants in Pinellas Park provide life-changing benefits that begin with improving your smile. Filling in those gaps allow you to feel your best each day, and there are also benefits for your oral health. Most people's oral hygiene improves when they feel motivated to care for their new smile, and those implanted posts help to stimulate your jawbone, which reduces bone loss over time.

Which Type of Implant Is Best for My Needs?

In addition to subperiosteal and endosteal implants, we've got several other types that you can pick from to create a custom smile.

* Implant-supported bridge
* Single implant

Taking Care of Your New Implants

When it comes to caring for an implant, you'll find that the steps you'll need to take fit right in with your normal oral hygiene routine. Unlike with dentures, you don't take implants out. Instead, you'll use your toothbrush to clean the crown. Then, you'll floss around the post to remove food debris that gets stuck between your teeth. Then, you'll stick to regular checkups with your dentist to make sure they heal properly and stay in good health for years to come.

What Makes You a Strong Candidate for a Dental Implant?

Determining who needs implants begins with a visit to the dentist. You already may be a good candidate for an implant if you prefer to have a full smile or feel uncomfortable with missing teeth no matter where they are in your mouth. Strong candidates also have good oral health, or they are motivated to improve issues that include gum disease.

How Long Do Implants Last on Average?

There isn't a definite answer to the question of how long does a dental implant last, but we can get pretty close. The average implant lasts about 10 years or more, and the success of your implant mostly depends upon controllable factors that include staying on top of your oral hygiene. When you come to our dental clinic, we'll help you brush up on oral health care strategies that help implant procedures be a success.

What Is a Dental Filling?

A dental filling is commonly referred to as a tooth filling. It is a substance that is used to restore a tooth affected by decay back to its normal shape and function. When a dentist places a filling, he or she will remove the decayed tooth material. The tooth will then be properly cleaned before a filling made of porcelain, gold or some other substance is placed in the tooth. Fillings help protect teeth from becoming more decayed or damaged.

What Are Tooth Crowns and Dental Bridges?

Crowns and bridges are specific types of permanent prosthetic devices that are affixed to the teeth via high-bond dental cement and that can only be removed by a dentist. Crowns for teeth are commonly referred to as dental caps. This is because they are placed over the top of the teeth. A tooth bridge is a type of device that attaches to the teeth on either side of a gap, with pontic teeth in between.

What Type of Dentist Provides Tooth Fillings, Crowns, and Bridges?

If you need a filling, crown or a bridge, you can visit your regular dentist. After he or she has examined your teeth, gums and mouth, a recommendation for treatment will be made based on your individual needs.

How Much Does a Filling, Dental Bridge, or Tooth Crown Cost?

Fillings, crowns, and bridges are all custom-made devices, therefore the exact cost will differ between patients. There are many different things that determine what a person will have to pay for their restorative treatment. These things include the location of the work being done, the materials utilized, and if you have dental insurance. After your initial examination, your dentist will provide you with an estimate of your tooth filling cost, dental bridge cost, or dental crown cost.

What Kind of Tooth Fillings Can I Get?

While there are several types of fillings that you can get, your dentist will advise you on the type of tooth filling that will work best for you and your tooth. Some options are able to blend into your teeth. Popular types of fillings are porcelain, tooth-colored composite, silver amalgam, and gold.

What Kind of Tooth Crowns Can I Get?

A tooth crown can also be constructed from different materials. Ceramic, porcelain-fused-to-metal, and gold alloy are the most popular types of dental crown materials. The exact type your dentist will use will depend on where the tooth is located. For example, ceramic crowns are typically used for your front teeth, while gold crowns are placed in the back of the mouth.

What Kind of Dental Bridge Can I Get?

Our dentists also offer different types of tooth bridges. A traditional tooth bridge is usually created with a crown for an implant or adjoining teeth. A row of pontic teeth is then used to fill the gap created by the missing tooth or teeth.

What Can I Expect During a Procedure for a Crown?

In most cases, you can expect your procedure for your dental crown to take place over two visits. At your first appointment, your dentist will shape and prepare the affected tooth. He or she will make a mold of your tooth. This mold is used to create your final crown. A temporary crown will be placed over the tooth until your permanent one comes in. Your second appointment is where your dentist will place the crown over the tooth with dental cement. Each part of the procedure takes around 30 minutes to an hour to finish.

What Can I Expect During a Procedure for a Bridge?

It usually takes two appointments to have a bridge installed. During the first visit, your dentist will scrape off a portion of the enamel from the teeth of the abutment teeth. An impression of the teeth will be made so that your bridge and crowns can be custom fit. You will wear a temporary bridge until then. Your second visit consists of your dentist installing the bridge and ensuring that it fits comfortably in your mouth.

The inflammation from periodontal disease is also linked to high blood pressure and heart disease. Gum disease isn't just important for healthy teeth, it is important for a healthy body.

## Teeth whitening

Professional teeth whitening in a dentist's office in Pinellas Park, also called teeth bleaching, is a popular cosmetic dentistry procedure your teeth bleaching dentist can perform using a variety of different tools and techniques.

Alternatively, you can also perform teeth whitening at home yourself using trays custom-made by your dentist. These allow you to apply a powerful gel to your teeth while you're awake or sleeping.

In addition, a variety of home-use products for teeth whitening are also sold in most drugstores and grocery stores for self-application. These include over-the-counter teeth whitening gels, strips, chewing gums, paint-on films, mouth rinses, and toothpastes. (Note that whitening toothpastes containing peroxides don't remain on the teeth for enough time to have much of a whitening effect.)

At Florida Dental Centers Pinellas Park, your Pinellas Park teeth bleaching dentist will let you know whether to use an at-home teeth whitening system under his or her supervision or have him or her provide you with an in-office bleaching.

Types of Stains

There are two main types of stains, or tooth discolorations, and different tooth whitening systems eliminate either one or both of them.

The first type is surface stains, or extrinsic stains. These commonly occur due to colored compounds accumulating on the tooth enamel. The factors causing these stains are usually environmental or behavior and may include being exposed to copper, iron or other metal salts, smoking tobacco products, or consuming heavily pigmented foods and beverages, such as dark fruits, coffee, tea, sodas and red wine. Poor dental hygiene can also exacerbate these stains in terms of severity and color. Brushing your teeth with a whitening toothpaste can sometimes be enough to help effectively eliminate these discolorations, though not always. They may also only be partially effective in removing surface stains and won't be effective at all in removing the other type of tooth discoloration, known as intrinsic stains.

Intrinsic stains are located inside the teeth, either within the tooth enamel or in the dentin underlying it. These can be caused by systemic factors like genetic disorders, aging, or issues with tooth development following their eruption into the oral cavity. They may also be caused by the use in childhood of certain antibiotics or after using antiseptic mouth rinses for a prolonged period of time.

In-Office Teeth Bleaching Products and Procedures Available Through Your Pinellas Park Dentist

There are a variety of teeth whitening systems you can obtain through your dentist in Pinellas Park, including custom-fit trays that deliver whitening gels to your teeth. You can either use these at home or have your dentist apply them in-office. If your dentist applies a peroxide gel to your teeth to whiten them, he or she may also use a light or laser in order to enhance or accelerate the whitening process.

Alternatively, your dentist may perform a power-bleaching procedure which makes use of concentrated hydrogen peroxide solutions applied to the teeth for up to a half hour. The dentist may or may not include light activation in this treatment as well.

Instead of whitening your teeth for you in-office, your dentist might recommend a dentist-supervised, at-home teeth whitening approach. Options for these include professional products supplied and possibly applied by your dentist and non-professional products supplied over-the-counter at stores and applied yourself at home.

The teeth bleaching cost of over-the-counter products is generally the least out of all the options for teeth whitening in Pinellas Park, but they also tend to come with a trade-off in time compared with in-office treatments or even treatments your dentist provides for you to perform at home. Over-the-counter bleaching systems take approximately two weeks to achieve the same level of whitening as a dentist-provided, home-use tray system achieves in seven days and an in-office whitening achieves in a single, one-hour session.

Be aware that teeth whitening treatments may make your teeth become sensitive to extremely cold or hot temperatures. They can also cause short-term gum irritation. If you experience any of these side effects and they don't disappear within several days, visit your dentist in Pinellas Park as soon as possible.

Make sure you always follow the directions on any teeth whitening product you use and any instructions your dentist gives you for using such products. This way, you avoid doing your teeth and gums any harm from the treatment. If you feel extreme sensitivity or if your mouth develops sores, stop using any teeth whitening products immediately and contact your Pinellas Park dentist.

Is an Extraction My Only Choice?

Your dentist will always endeavor to salvage a natural tooth, but sometimes that's just not possible. In fact, sometimes a relatively healthy tooth will need to be pulled. The following examples can help explain why sometimes an extraction is the only option.

### Primary Teeth

The primary teeth are often colloquially referred to as baby teeth, and are the first set of teeth to appear. They usually fall out on their own starting around age four or five and will fall out in the same order they came in. However, sometimes the primary tooth doesn't automatically fall out, which doesn't allow the permanent tooth to come in, so the primary tooth will need to be extracted.

### Crowding

An adult mouth will usually have 32 teeth, but there's not always room for that many teeth in the jaw. When this happens, teeth may erupt at an angle or not at all, and the other teeth may become misaligned. If a permanent tooth can't fully erupt, it can become impacted and painful. The solution is to remove it even though it may not be diseased or damaged.

### Wisdom Teeth

The wisdom teeth are the third and final set of molars to appear, and they start erupting in the late teens to early twenties. By this time, however, there may not be enough room in the jaw, and you'll have an impacted wisdom tooth. The solution is to extract the impacted tooth or teeth.

Who Does Tooth Extractions?

If your tooth is readily visible and we're able to grasp it with forceps, your dentist can extract your tooth. If it's impacted or severely damaged, you may need a root canal, and we'll refer you to an oral surgeon.

Who Can Extract a Severely Damaged, Cracked, or Decayed Tooth?

If your tooth is badly diseased or damaged, your Pinellas Park dentist may be able to extract it. Otherwise, you'll need to see an oral surgeon to have it removed. General dentists can perform routine oral surgery, but specialty cases are usually referred to a specialist. There needs to be enough tooth structure for the dentist to grasp with forceps.

Can I Have a Tooth Pulled if I Have Advanced Gum Disease?

If you're in the advanced stage of periodontal disease, you may have already lost a significant number of teeth. However, if you have a tooth that's causing problems, your Pinellas Park dentist may be able to extract it. Call our Pinellas Park office for an appointment or if you have more questions.

How Much Will My Tooth Extraction Cost?

Your cost for a tooth extraction will be unique to you and will depend on the complexity of the procedure, the number of follow-up visits you'll need, and your insurance coverage. Typically, insurance plans will pay for all or part of getting a tooth pulled, but check with your provider before your appointment. We'll provide you with a detailed estimate of the cost of your procedure, but if you have questions, call the office.

What is the Aftercare Procedure for an Extraction?

We'll provide you with aftercare instructions appropriate to your procedure, and it's important that you follow them to the letter. Otherwise, your clot can break open or become dislodged, and then you'll start bleeding again. We'll also include instructions for minimizing swelling and discomfort. The first 24 hours are the most critical, so adhere to the aftercare instructions assiduously during the first 24 hours. If you experience problems or have questions, call the office, and we'll be glad to help you.

What's the Tooth Extraction Healing Time?

There's no set time for a tooth to heal, but your age and overall health are factors, as is your unique physiology and how well you follow your aftercare instructions. If you had a simple tooth extraction, you may be able to resume moderate activities after the first 24 hours, but ask your dentist if you need to engage in strenuous activities. If you had oral surgery or a molar extraction, the site will usually take longer to heal. Call us if you have questions.

# Medicare advantage dental benefits in Pinellas Park (Seniors 65+)

Traditional Medicare, the plan that comes with the red, white, and blue ID card, does not provide coverage for basic dental services, such as exams, cleanings, and fillings. Traditional Medicare will only cover dental services under limited circumstances when they are required as part of a service or procedure covered under Medicare Part A hospital benefits, such as when a dental exam is required as part of pre-surgery clearance. Medicare recipients must look elsewhere for help in paying for preventive, maintenance, or restorative dental services.

## What You Need to Know About Dental Coverage Before Enrolling in Medicare Advantage in Pinellas Park

Even though they are typically more likely than the general population to require dental care, approximately 65% of seniors do not have dental insurance. There are a couple of reasons for this. First, seniors are automatically enrolled in government-sponsored Medicare when they reach the age of 65. Second, most people receive their dental coverage through their employer, which means that they lose it once they retire and leave the workforce.

The lack of affordable insurance options that cover dental expenses is likely to be a major health issue in the coming years since tens of thousands of baby boomers reach the age of 65 or retire every day. For example:

* Approximately 6 million more seniors visited a dentist during 2016 than in 2006.
* In 2016 alone, seniors spent more than $28 billion on dental services.
* The rate of spending for dental services was higher among seniors than any other segment of the population.
* Approximately half of all Medicare recipients did not seek out dental services in the past year. This is due in large part to the lack of insurance coverage.

## What Is the Average Cost for Dental Services Without Dental Insurance?

The cost of dental services varies based on location; however, even a relatively minor procedure can easily run into the hundreds or even thousands of dollars. According to the Kaiser Family Foundation, 19% of Medicare recipients who visit the dentist end up spending more than $1,000 out of pocket. The following are the average costs for some of the most common dental procedures:

### Checkups and Cleanings

* Basic exam-$50 to $100
* Dental X-ray-$20 to $250
* Standard cleaning-$70 to $200

### Fillings

* Silver amalgam-$50 to $300
* Composite-$90 to $450

### Extractions

* Simple extraction-$75 to $450
* Surgical extraction-$150 to $650
* Wisdom tooth extraction-$75 to $3,000 based on the number and complexity of the extractions

### Crowns

The cost of a crown can range from $500 to $3,000 based on the type of material used.

### Root Canals

The cost of a root canal can range from $300 to $2,000 based on the location of the tooth and the complexity of the procedure.

## What Are the Different Types of Dental Benefits in the Tampa Bay area?

Approximately 25% of seniors enroll in a Medicare Advantage supplement plan while 10% opt to purchase comprehensive coverage through a private insurer. Some patients also take advantage of discount plans or financing options that can be used in place of or in conjunction with insurance.

## What Types of Expenses Are Covered Under Medicare Advantage?

Medicare Advantage plans are optional plans that are purchased by the Medicare recipient to expand on the benefits provided under traditional Medicare. Unlike standard Medicare where health care providers are reimbursed by the government, supplemental plans are offered and reimbursed by private insurers, such as UHC, Aetna, and Humana. This also means that you will get a separate ID card from the insurer. Medicare Advantage plans do have a number of benefits, including:

* access to a qualified network of health care providers,
* out of pocket spending limits, and
* low deductibles.

With a low average cost per year, Medicare supplement plans are relatively affordable. In addition to covering X-rays, exams, cleanings, and other basic dental services, these plans also normally include prescription, vision, hearing, and other wellness benefits.

## How Does Standalone Dental Insurance Work?

If you have significant oral health issues or want the peace of mind of knowing that you have comprehensive dental coverage, you may want to consider a standalone dental policy. Most standalone dental plans offer tiered coverage, which means that basic services are covered at 100%, basic procedures at 80%, and complex procedures at 50%. With standalone coverage, you typically have the flexibility of choosing from several different levels of coverage with various benefits and price points.

## Which Type of Standalone Dental Insurance Should I Choose?

Most private dental insurers offer three levels of coverage:

### Basic Plans

This plan is suitable for individuals who tend to only see the dentist for basic maintenance and preventative care. Basic plans normally cover X-rays, exams, cleanings, and preventative services.

### Mid-level Plans

Unless you are likely to need advanced dental care, mid-level plans offer a nice mix of expanded services to cover most common dental issues. For example, this type of plan typically offers benefits for specialized X-rays, fillings, dentures, inhalation anesthesia, emergency treatment, and even orthodontics.

### Premium Plans

Premium dental plans typically offer at least partial coverage for even more advanced treatments and procedures, including endodontic and periodontic procedures, oral surgery, crowns, inlays and onlays, and complete or partial dentures.

## How Do Dental Discount Plans Work?

Although they are not insurance, dental service discount plans are an affordable alternative to Medicare supplements or private insurance for some individuals. Instead of a premium, discount plans charge a low enrollment and monthly membership fee. In return, members receive special discounted rates at participating providers. In addition to being affordable, discount plans have a number of other advantages:

* You pay the provider directly, so there are no claim forms to fill out.
* Discount plans normally accept anyone regardless of age or pre-existing conditions.
* There are no exclusion periods, so you can use your benefits right away.
* You don't have to worry about copays, deductibles, or coinsurance obligations.
* There are no restrictions on the number of times that you can use your benefits during the year.
* You are free to change providers at any time instead of having to wait for the next enrollment period.
* Most discount plans also provide discounts for prescriptions, hearing and vision services, and other wellness services.

While discount plans, such as Smile Alliance Club, offer significant discounts on services ranging from checkups to root canals, they are most appropriate for individuals who are in good oral health and unlikely to need advanced dental work. A comprehensive insurance plan may save you more money if you are likely to need extensive dental work.

Even without a Medicare supplement, private insurance, or discount plan, there are still ways to make the cost of dental services more manageable. Many dental providers now offer flexible payment options and financing options. What Is the Meaning of Root Canals or Root Canal Treatment?

Many types of tooth pain are easily treatable without having to go too far beyond the surface of your tooth enamel. A very small cavity might not cause any pain at all, or you might feel a short burst of discomfort that goes away soon after a cold bite of food leaves your mouth. Sadly, some types of dental issues don't go away so easily. When dental pulp gets inflamed or infected for a variety of different reasons, it can cause steady, severe pain that is only treatable with root canals. Removing the injured pulp is what root canals are all about, and dentists only recommend them when they are necessary for bringing you long-term comfort.

When Do Dentists Recommend Root Canals?

You might already suspect that you need major dental work if you've been coping with chronic tooth pain. A root canal dentist usually recommends this type of treatment when you are experiencing severe pain, especially if it keeps you up at night or is caused by a deep cavity or broken tooth. Sometimes, infections from the pulp work their way into the gums, which could cause swelling and the appearance of a boil. People with pulp inflammation also find it hard to eat without pain, and you might catch yourself trying to only chew on one side of your mouth to avoid a sudden shock of discomfort. When you visit our office presenting with these symptoms, our dentist will do a visual exam and imaging tests to look for signs of infection or irritation in the tooth and surrounding tissues.

Can Any Dentist Do Root Canals?

For many people, it simply feels more emotionally comfortable to visit a general dentist that you've been seeing for years. The good news is that general dentists are usually perfectly capable of performing successful root canals, which gives you more options for finding someone that puts you at ease. If you need a repeat procedure on the same tooth you had work done on before, then you might be referred to an endodontist. This type of dentist has undergone additional training regarding performing oral surgeries that involve the tooth root, and they'll be just as good at helping you to feel comfortable as your regular dental provider. If you're stuck on searching for a dentist, then call our office to find the perfect one to get you started on improving your comfort.

What Are the Primary Parts of a Root Canal Procedure?

As you might've guessed, root canals involve several critical steps that all help to prep your tooth and get it healthy again. Some of the following steps may be familiar, since they are commonly performed during other types of dental procedures. If you have a question about any part, then remember that we are always ready to give you the answers you need to proceed with confidence.

* Using numbing agents and anesthesia to keep you free from pain
* Clean and surround the tooth with a special shield to protect it during the procedure
* Make a hole through the biting surface of the tooth to reach the tooth root
* Remove the pulp and clean the canals before flushing them to remove leftover debris
* Use gutta-percha, a special rubbery material, to seal the hole and canals
* Top off the tooth with a root canal crown

Is There a Wide Range for the Root Canal Cost?

The cost for a dental root canal varies from one provider to another. Your dentist may also base the price on the location of the tooth that requires care. Molars contain four roots, which will cost more to clean out compared to a front tooth with one. Most dental insurance providers cover at least part of the cost for your care. We'll work with you to make sure that you have the financing you need to get your painful tooth fixed.

Are There Different Types of Root Canals?

An apicoectomy is a special type of oral surgery that functions like a root canal, but the tip of the root is removed to provide long-term pain relief for repeated root canals. Pediatric pulpotomies are another type that leaves the nerve in place while still removing all of the tooth pulp. While most people get standard root canals, it helps to know about these special kinds in case your dentist recommends them for handling your personal needs.

How Do You Start Planning for Dental Root Canal Treatment?

If you're the type that likes to have a plan, then you'll love knowing that getting a root canal in Pinellas Park is a straightforward process. All you need to do to get started on making plans is contact our office for your first appointment. We'll take it all from there by making sure that you are comfortable in our chair and understand each part of your recommended treatment plan.
